correctness.rationale: The source proof was reconstructed at the rate step: it establishes a finite sum of weighted squared increments and obtains \(\min_{j\le k}Q_j=o(1/k)\) by a tail-averaging argument. Taking square roots yields only \(\min_{j\le k}\sqrt{Q_j}=o(k^{-1/2})\). The explicit sequence \(z_k=1/\log(k+2)\) converges, has square-summable increments of order \(1/[k^2(\log k)^4]\), and therefore satisfies the same best squared-increment premise, but \(kz_k\to\infty\), including along every subsequence. Thus the claimed iterate-rate implication is invalid without an additional error-bound relation.
